learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the colorful traditional art of binding fabric to create beautiful, unique, and vibrant patterns using basic materials and dyes!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Tie and dye is a special 'resist' technique. When you tie a piece of cloth tightly with thread or rubber bands, the dye cannot reach those folded areas. Once you open it up, the tied parts stay white, creating amazing patterns!

You do not need a fancy workshop! All you need is a plain white cotton cloth, strong thread or rubber bands, a bucket, and some colorful dyes. You can even use natural kitchen dyes like turmeric (yellow) or beetroot (pink).

There are many fun ways to tie your cloth! The 'Spiral' creates a cool swirl, 'Crumple' gives a messy marble look, and the traditional Indian 'Bandhani' uses tiny, tight knots to create beautiful dotted designs.

First, wash the cloth. Second, fold and tie it tightly. Third, dip it carefully into the dye bath and let it soak. Finally, rinse it with cold water, cut the threads, and unfold your magical masterpiece!

fun_activity.title: 💛 The Turmeric Handkerchief Trick!
fun_activity.instructions: Take an old white cotton handkerchief, pinch the center, and tie three rubber bands tightly along the fabric. Soak it in warm water mixed with a spoon of turmeric powder for 30 minutes, then rinse and untie for a bright yellow sunburst!

quick_recap: ⭐ Tie and dye is a 'resist' technique where tied areas block the color from soaking in.
⭐ Plain cotton is the best fabric to use because it absorbs dyes very easily.
⭐ Different tying methods like spiraling, folding, and knotting create completely different patterns.
⭐ Natural materials like turmeric and onion skins can be used as eco-friendly dyes.
⭐ Always rinse the dyed fabric in cold water before opening the knots to set the color.
